chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Song titles of the 1920s blues and their later recordings
summary: Hinton and Jones discuss which tracks to play and how Black artists' songs were named after people and places in the 1920s.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Well, do you think that we should play some more of these, like the Dirty Dozen, "When the Sun Goes Down," "Hey Lordy Mama," "The Fives," "Oh Red" and "Dupree Blues". Which one of these do you think we should play?
Well, either one you play because all these

were conducive, is the way the Negro artist had to do. They put characters - they name these songs after peoples, as in the later years when we came through they said "Swingin' It at the Ritz". You know, that was the Ritz Hotel. 'Stompin' at the Savoy" and etcetera. These things and those things, this is in the 20's.
We'll put all tracks of these on here. We'll put the next 6 tracks on and then we'll go to the 40's, because this is all the 30's.
This is in the 20's right now. All these blues are the 20's.
But these were recorded in the 30's.
Yes, but there's recapitulation there. All these things was updated.
